story_type: aircraft carrier high speed turns on sea trials
hook: An aircraft carrier, thrown into a turn at high speed.
narration: This aircraft carrier is leaning into a turn at high speed.
USS Gerald R. Ford had just spent fifteen months at a shipyard.
Crews repaired its main reduction gear and improved the controls that set its speed.
On October twenty ninth, the bridge team threw it into high speed turns.
Sea trials test the systems the shipyard repaired or changed.
[short pause] From above, the wake drew the whole curve behind it.
outcome: Ford finished the work on October thirtieth and went home to Norfolk.
title: Carrier leans into a high speed turn
description:
USS Gerald R. Ford (CVN 78) runs high speed turns in the Atlantic Ocean during sea trials, Oct. 29, 2019, after a 15-month shipyard period.

Footage: U.S. Navy video by Mass Communication Specialist 3rd Class Connor Loessin, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/718912/cvn-78-high-speed-turns

extra_sources.excerpt: NEWPORT NEWS, Va. — The aircraft carrier USS Gerald R. Ford got underway Oct. 25 for sea trials from Huntington Ingalls Industries’ Newport News Shipbuilding division following a 15-month pierside maintenance period. While at sea off the Virginia coast, the crew, in cooperation with NNS engineers and shipyard employees, will run through a comprehensive sequence of evolutions to test and validate systems maintained or modified during the extended maintenance period, known as a post-shakedown availability (PSA).

WASHINGTON — The aircraft carrier USS Gerald R. Ford is back in its homeport at Naval Station Norfolk, Virginia, after successful completion on Oct. 30 of its post-shakedown availability/selected restricted availability, Program Executive Office (PEO) Aircraft Carriers announced. CVN 78’s PSA began on July 15, 2018, and included work on Advanced Weapons Elevators (AWEs), repairs to the ship’s main reduction gear, improvements to the throttle control system, upgrades to the advanced arresting gear and numerous other maintenance tasks.
ATLANTIC OCEAN (Oct. 29, 2019) USS Gerald R. Ford's (CVN 78) bridge watch team conducts high speed turns as part of sea trials.
